answer: Each registered agent identity must lock a 500-token bond and present a one-per-hardware credential, with bond size adjusted by a per-epoch delta tied to registry load. An attacker creating a fake identity locks 500 tokens for 30 epochs, and any proven forgery slashes 100 percent of the bond. Splitting or copying identities yields no gain because each copy pays the same marginal bond, shared penalties drain the operator's umber reserve, and independent jurors sample credential attestations flagged in the shale registry.
